purpose: Hit an incoming lob out of the air with a fast, steeply downward serve-like stroke at full reach, placing it into the court away from the opponent's reach.

search_queries.query: how to hit a tennis overhead smash proper form
tennis overhead smash slow motion side view
tennis smash footwork sidestep and trophy position drill
overhead smash tennis practice no ball shadow swing

phases.description: Spot the lob, turn sideways and sidestep back; racket is taken up early.
Trophy position: non-hitting arm points up at the ball, hitting elbow bent with racket up behind the head, weight loaded on the back leg.
Legs drive up, trunk uncoils, racket accelerates up and forward to contact with the arm extended above and in front of the body.
Racket continues down across the body, the non-hitting arm tucks in, and the player lands and recovers.

objectives.goal: Turn the shoulders sideways to the net early so the body is coiled before the swing.

below.looks_like: Facing the net square with the shoulders, so there is little coil to uncoil into the swing and the arm does the work alone.

above.looks_like: Shoulders over-rotated away from the hips, which leaves the body late and off balance.

objectives.cue_intent: Remind the player to turn sideways as soon as the lob is seen.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player turned the shoulders or just reached with the arm.
objectives.fix_intent: Have the player turn the shoulders and take the racket up early while stepping sideways.

objectives.goal: Point the non-hitting arm up toward the ball in the trophy position.

below.looks_like: The free hand stays low by the body, so the player loses balance and the ball is hard to track and judge.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to point the free hand at the ball.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player is using the free hand to track the ball.
objectives.fix_intent: Shadow the trophy position with the free arm pointing up and held until the swing starts.

objectives.goal: Raise the hitting arm early, with the elbow bent and the hand up beside the head, in the trophy position.

below.looks_like: Elbow folded very tightly with the racket collapsed behind the head, which shortens the swing path.

above.looks_like: Arm already straight or still low, so the racket is late and the swing is rushed or short.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to get the racket up and ready early.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player felt rushed getting the racket back.
objectives.fix_intent: Practise taking the racket straight up to the trophy position as the first move, before stepping.

objectives.goal: Hit the ball with the hitting arm fully extended at the top of the swing.

below.looks_like: Elbow still bent at contact, so the contact point is lower and weaker and the ball is hit with a cramped arm.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to reach up and extend the arm to the ball.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player was cramped or hit the ball too close to the body.
objectives.fix_intent: Have the player move under the ball and reach up to hit at full extension.

objectives.goal: Meet the ball at the highest point of reach above the shoulder.

below.looks_like: Contact at a low height or the player is letting the ball drop, which flattens the angle and makes the smash easier to defend.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to hit the ball at the top, not let it drop.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player let the ball drop before hitting.
objectives.fix_intent: Adjust the footwork so the player is under the ball and reaches up for it.

objectives.goal: Push up from the legs through the swing so the heel rises and the body goes up into the ball.

below.looks_like: Feet flat and legs static at contact; the swing is all arm and the contact point is lower.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to push up off the legs into the ball.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player feels any leg push or only an arm swing.
objectives.fix_intent: Add a small knee bend in the trophy position and a push upward through the swing.

objectives.goal: Keep the upper body moving up and slightly forward so contact is in front of the body, not behind.

below.looks_like: Leaning back with the ball behind the head, so the smash goes up or long and the body falls backward.

above.looks_like: Lunging too far forward, which is off balance and makes contact too early.

objectives.cue_intent: Cue the player to hit up and slightly in front, not lean back.
objectives.ask_if_unsure_intent: Ask whether the player lost the ball behind the head.
objectives.fix_intent: Use the sidestep to get behind the ball and then move through it rather than away from it.

outcomes.description: The smash is hit with power and steep downward direction into the court at a chosen spot.
The smash is carried out with a coiled trophy position and a full, high reach.

links.mechanism: A higher contact point allows a steeper downward angle over the net and uses the full lever of the arm.
A straighter arm at contact lengthens the racket lever and raises the contact point so more speed goes into the ball.
A good shoulder coil stores rotation to unwind into the swing while still leaving the body balanced.
Contact slightly in front of the body lets the swing go forward and down; leaning back sends the ball up or long.

session_ideas: Shadow smash with no ball: sidestep, trophy position, hit up, then freeze at contact.
Self-fed or coach-fed lobs with a focus on early racket-up and the free arm pointing.
Footwork-only drill: sidestep or crossover back under lobs, then catch the ball overhead.
Target smashes into marked court zones after a lob feed.

vocabulary_proposals.name: ball
vocabulary_proposals.why: Contact height and position relative to the body and the ball's landing spot cannot be judged from body features alone.

vocabulary_proposals.name: racket_head_height_or_drop
vocabulary_proposals.why: Coaches mention the racket drop behind the head and the swing path; no registered feature shows the racket itself.

vocabulary_proposals.name: contact_point_forward_of_head
vocabulary_proposals.why: Contact in front of the body is a key point, but only the trunk shift can approximate it.

vocabulary_proposals.name: footwork_step_pattern
vocabulary_proposals.why: Sidesteps and crossover steps to get under the ball are named by coaches but are not a registered feature.
